videoIdeas.title: Why young Muslims can't hold a conversation
videoIdeas.hook: The amount of you who can't string a sentence together is genuinely alarming.
videoIdeas.rationale: Your own post on this exact topic (DbilFRjsJ3v) pulled 622 views with zero comments — the topic lands but the delivery didn't invite response. Public speaking is your weakest-populated pillar despite it being a named pillar. Saffana proves blunt, corrective 'you sound like X' hooks about communication do huge numbers. This is a gap you own.
videoIdeas.script: The amount of you who can't string a sentence together is genuinely alarming. And it's not a confidence thing — it's a practice thing. You've spent ten years typing and zero years talking. So when someone puts you on the spot, you freeze, you fill the gap with 'like' and 'you know', and you convince yourself you're just an introvert. You're not. You're unpracticed. Speaking is a skill, same as any other. You don't get better by reading about it, you get better by opening your mouth in rooms where it's uncomfortable. Order your own food. Ask the question in the lecture. Speak in the group chat's real-life equivalent. The brothers who lead anything all have one thing in common — they can talk. Start being one of them.

visuals.setting: Talking straight to camera, mid-shot, plain wall or café corner, calm but firm energy — no pacing, no hype. Casual smart: plain crew neck or overshirt.
visuals.visualHook: On-screen text 'You're not an introvert. You're unpracticed.' slams up on the first frame while you hold a flat, unimpressed expression for a half-second before speaking.
otherHookIdeas: Cold open mid-sentence with you imitating the 'like… you know… basically' filler, then cut hard to you speaking clean
Pattern interrupt: hold up your phone, then set it face-down on the table as you say the first line
On-screen text punchline delayed to the end: 'Speaking is a skill. Go practice.'

videoIdeas.title: Competent and trustworthy — the leadership order everyone gets wrong
videoIdeas.hook: You want influence before you've earned character. That's backwards.
videoIdeas.rationale: Your prophetic-leadership post (DTauCL6jJ8Z) did 508 with strong likes (58) — the framing resonates but the caption buried the point. Leadership is a core pillar that's underrepresented in your top posts versus your Ummah commentary. Doctordaanish's 'save this' advice format proves prescriptive, quotable leadership content travels. Repackage your best idea into a sharper single-point video.
videoIdeas.script: You want influence before you've earned character. That's backwards, and it's why so many of these accounts collapse the second they're tested. The Prophetic model — peace be upon him — gives the order plainly: Al-Qawi wal-Ameen. Strong and trustworthy. Competent and honest. Notice the sequence people skip: trust comes before reach. We've flipped it. Everyone's building an audience before they've built a spine. So you get people with a hundred thousand followers who can't be trusted to hold a secret, let alone a community. Don't chase the platform. Become the kind of person a platform would be safe in your hands. The influence follows the character. It never works the other way round.

visuals.setting: Seated, slightly closer framing, warmer setting — bookshelf or masjid-adjacent backdrop. Measured, deliberate delivery. Modest smart clothing.
visuals.visualHook: On-screen text 'Al-Qawi wal-Ameen' appears in clean Arabic + English as you say the first line, so the concept anchors visually in the first 3 seconds.
otherHookIdeas: Cold open on the phrase 'Trust comes before reach' before you introduce yourself
Prop: hold a book, close it and set it down on 'Don't chase the platform'
Two-word on-screen counter — 'Character.' then 'Then influence.' — cutting in on the beat

videoIdeas.title: Stop refuting people and build something
videoIdeas.hook: Half of you would rather win an argument than build anything.
videoIdeas.rationale: Your 'third spaces' post (Dbwq4JosFxD) and your 'is it not time to focus on what's dire' post both show your audience responds to a build-don't-bicker message. You even admitted you didn't want your page to be a refutation page (DZCxYL9MFMb). Turn that self-awareness into a mindset piece — it's on-brand, timely, and pivots your commentary energy into something constructive.
videoIdeas.script: Half of you would rather win an argument than build anything. I get it — refuting people feels productive. You typed the paragraph, you got the likes, you felt right. But being right in a comment section has never fed a single family or opened a single space. Look at what's actually working: young Muslims building cafés, study circles, community hubs — real places where people belong. That's worth more than a thousand takedowns. Every hour you spend proving someone wrong online is an hour you didn't spend making something that outlives the argument. Ask yourself honestly: at the end of the year, what did you build? Not what did you win. What did you build. If the answer is nothing, the problem was never them.

visuals.setting: Filmed in or outside a café / community space if possible — ties the message to the visual. Standing, relaxed, real-world energy. Everyday clothes.
visuals.visualHook: Cold open walking into a busy café/community space, camera following, on-screen text: 'This beats winning an argument.'
otherHookIdeas: Pattern interrupt: mime typing furiously on a phone, then toss it aside on the first line
On-screen text punchline held to the close: 'What did you build?'
Cut between a comment-section screenshot and a real space to show the contrast

videoIdeas.title: Read this before you speak in public again
videoIdeas.hook: Save this if the thought of speaking in front of people makes you want to disappear.
videoIdeas.rationale: Doctordaanish's 'if you're in your 20s pls save this' listicle format hit 34k+ and drives huge saves. You have no save-optimised content in your top posts. A tight, numbered public speaking listicle fills a pillar gap and taps a format proven in your niche right now.
videoIdeas.script: Save this if the thought of speaking in front of people makes you want to disappear. Three things, quickly. One: nobody can see your nerves as loudly as you feel them. The shaking you're convinced is obvious is invisible to the room. Two: slow down. When you panic you speed up, and speeding up makes you sound less sure. A deliberate pause reads as authority — use it. Three: stop trying to sound impressive. The moment you're focused on impressing, you're thinking about yourself, not your message. Talk to them like you'd talk to one person you respect. That's it. You don't need to be a natural. You need reps and a message you actually believe in. Everything else is just practice.

visuals.setting: Clean, direct-to-camera, mid-shot, higher energy than the mindset pieces but still controlled. Numbers can appear as you count them.
visuals.visualHook: Big on-screen text 'SAVE THIS' with a subtle number counter '1 / 2 / 3' preview flashing in the first frame to signal a listicle.
otherHookIdeas: Cold open on point 2 — 'Slow. Down.' — then rewind to the intro
Each tip gets its own bold on-screen card so viewers screenshot
Pattern interrupt: pretend to shake nervously, then straighten up as you say 'nobody can see your nerves'

videoIdeas.title: Has the Muslim influencer lost the plot?
videoIdeas.hook: Has the Muslim influencer completely lost the plot?
videoIdeas.rationale: Lifeofdinoo's short provocative-question videos ('Has University Lost Its Prestige?', 'What's the long-term play here?') are pulling 17k–37k right now — the open-question format is working in your exact niche. You already write provocative commentary; frame it as an open question to invite the comments your posts sometimes lack (e.g. your 885-view post got 0 comments).
videoIdeas.script: Has the Muslim influencer completely lost the plot? Genuine question. Because somewhere along the way, the goal stopped being benefit and started being reach. The UAE hijrah content, the constant refutations, the flexing dressed up as da'wah — none of it is actually for you. It's for the algorithm. And the strange part is we keep rewarding it. We follow, we engage, we argue, and then we wonder why the content only gets shallower. You vote with your attention every single day. So here's the real question — not for them, for you: what are you actually giving your time to, and is it making you better or just keeping you busy? Tell me I'm wrong.

visuals.setting: Direct to camera, slightly raised eyebrow energy, conversational not preachy. Neutral background. The question format should feel like you're genuinely asking.
visuals.visualHook: Full-screen text card 'Has the Muslim influencer lost the plot?' on a plain background for the first 2 seconds — mirrors the dinoo question format that's working.
otherHookIdeas: End on the on-screen question 'Making you better, or keeping you busy?' to drive comments
Cold open on 'Tell me I'm wrong.' then cut back to the start
Pattern interrupt: scroll a feed on your phone, look up unimpressed, then speak

videoIdeas.title: The leader everyone follows but nobody respects
videoIdeas.hook: There's a difference between someone people follow and someone people respect. Most 'leaders' only have one.
videoIdeas.rationale: Leadership is a named pillar but only appears deep in your top posts. Your audience clearly responds to Prophetic-framed, character-first messaging (your leadership and hadith posts hold strong like ratios). A clean single-idea leadership piece with a sharp contrast hook is a gap and plays to your strength of articulate, principled takes.
videoIdeas.script: There's a difference between someone people follow and someone people respect. Most so-called leaders only have one. You can gather a following through noise — be loud enough, controversial enough, confident enough, and people will watch. But watching isn't respect. Respect is what people give you when you're not in the room. It's built quietly: keeping your word when it costs you, giving credit you could have taken, staying steady when everyone else is panicking. Following is loud and fast. Respect is slow and silent. And here's the uncomfortable bit — you can have thousands following you and not a single person who'd trust you with something that matters. Don't confuse the two. Build the one that lasts.

visuals.setting: Seated, closer and calmer framing, low-key confident. Softer lighting, evening feel. Measured delivery — let lines land.
visuals.visualHook: On-screen text splits the screen: 'FOLLOWED' vs 'RESPECTED' as you deliver the opening contrast.
otherHookIdeas: Cold open on 'Respect is what people give you when you're not in the room.'
On-screen text punchline at the close: 'Followed ≠ Respected'
Pause-and-hold beat after 'Most leaders only have one' before continuing

postSuggestions.whatsWorking: This is your standout — 6134 views, more than double your next best. The hook 'Can't believe we're still discussing the necessity of protests in 2026' is dated, urgent and instantly divisive, which is exactly why it travelled. Your blunt commentary voice is fully switched on here and the topic is genuinely time-sensitive.
postSuggestions.whatToImprove: 15 comments on 6134 views is low for a topic this charged — the caption is a statement, not an opening. End with a direct question or a line people feel compelled to answer ('Tell me why that's wrong'), and the algorithm will push a post like this even further.

postSuggestions.whatsWorking: This is your public speaking pillar showing up — 'The amount of people that struggle to string a sentence together is shocking' is a strong, blunt, older-brother hook that's on-brand and fills your under-served pillar. It's the kind of corrective take that's working for competitors like Saffana.
postSuggestions.whatToImprove: 622 views and zero comments means the delivery didn't match the hook's promise. The caption drifts into 'back in the days people would go outside' nostalgia, which softens the point. Keep it prescriptive — tell them exactly what to do about it (order your own food, ask the question in the lecture) so it becomes a save-and-share, not a rant.

postSuggestions.whatsWorking: Genuinely your best pillar content: 'We often chase influence before character' is a crisp, quotable single idea, and the 58 likes on 508 views is one of your strongest like-to-view ratios — meaning the people who saw it valued it. Al-Qawi wal-Ameen is a memorable anchor.
postSuggestions.whatToImprove: The caption turns into a carousel-style '11 Prophetic Qualities of Leadership' list, which splits focus. One video, one idea. Cut it to just the character-before-influence point, drive harder on the hook, and this deserves far more than 508 views — it's underexposed, not underperforming.

postSuggestions.whatsWorking: The 'young British Muslims are creating third spaces' angle is constructive, specific and positive — a refreshing break from refutation content, and the concrete examples (cafés, study circles, community hubs) give it substance. This is the kind of build-something message your audience should associate with you.
postSuggestions.whatToImprove: 894 views but only 2 comments — a positive post like this needs an ask. You're describing something people are proud of; invite them to name their local space or tag it. Also the hook is descriptive, not provocative — lead with the tension ('People keep telling young Muslims to stop building. They're wrong') to earn the scroll-stop.

postSuggestions.whatsWorking: 24 comments on 2997 views is one of your highest engagement rates — the Iraq/Afghanistan/Iran hook taps real anger and the parallel structure ('under the same guise') is sharp writing. When you draw a clean historical line, people show up to debate.
postSuggestions.whatToImprove: This kind of geopolitical commentary drives comments but sits outside your three stated pillars (leadership, public speaking, mindset). It's fine as a spike, but lean the same debate-sparking structure into your pillars — apply that 'they did X under the guise of Y' framing to leadership or mindset topics so the engagement compounds your actual niche instead of pulling away from it.
